original_question: If X is a class of groups, let H(X) denote the class of homomorphic images of groups in X, let S(X) denote the class of groups isomorphic to subgroups of groups in X, let P(X) denote the class of groups isomorphic to(unrestricted) direct products of families of groups in X, and let Pf(X) denote the class of groups isomorphic to direct products of finite families of groups in X. By Birkhoff’s theorem, H(S(P(X))) is the variety of groups generated by X. If M is a class of metabelian groups, must H(S(Pf(M))) ⊆ S(H(P(S(M))))? This is Question 27 in(G. M. Bergman, Algebra Universalis, 26(1989), 267–283).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.17 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)", which reproduces Bergman's Question 27 from Algebra Universalis 26 (1989), 267–283. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is essentially verbatim the official formulation in the paper: it correctly defines the operators H, S, P, and Pf on classes of groups; correctly specifies that P means unrestricted direct products and Pf finite direct products; correctly inserts the Birkhoff-theorem context that H(S(P(X))) is the variety generated by X; and correctly asks the inclusion for an arbitrary class M of metabelian groups. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
refined_question: Let M be a class of metabelian groups. For any class X of groups, write H(X) for the class of homomorphic images of groups in X, S(X) for the class of groups isomorphic to subgroups of groups in X, P(X) for the class of groups isomorphic to unrestricted direct products of families of groups in X, and Pf(X) for the class of groups isomorphic to direct products of finite families of groups in X. Since, by Birkhoff’s theorem, H(S(P(X))) is the variety of groups generated by X, must one always have H(S(Pf(M))) ⊆ S(H(P(S(M))))? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
